title: Efficiency Assistant: progressive onboarding canvases and annotated screenshot pack for batching/caching & quantization
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Produce a compact, developer-focused onboarding experience for the Optimize Toolkit that surfaces batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization recommendations. Deliver a set of progressive canvases (3 mobile / 4 desktop), an annotated screenshot library for docs and the Console release notes, and two microcopy variants for A/B copy testing. These assets will be used in: the in-product first-run flow, the Optimize quickstart doc, and the release blog post.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 3 responsive onboarding canvases (desktop wide, narrow, mobile) exported in production-ready PNG/SVG with layered Figma file. 2) Annotated screenshot pack (12 images) covering: batch size slider, autoscaling hint, KV cache enablement, cache hit-rate indicator, quant profile selector with example latency/cost estimate. Each image must include frame-level callouts and short copy for docs. 3) Two microcopy variants (technical-first, outcomes-first) for all screen headings and CTAs. 4) Figma prototype with click-through for PM/Eng review. 5) File naming and asset manifest uploaded to drive folder and linked in PR. 6) Accessibility check notes (color contrast, alt text) documented.
design_notes:
- Prioritize developer mental models: show "what changes" (latency/cost/quality) with small numeric examples rather than abstract terms.
- Use simplified chart sparingly: a sparkline comparing token-cost with/without batching and with quantization.
- Keep CTAs consistent: primary action is 'Apply recommendations', secondary 'Preview impact'.
- For KV cache, highlight prefix examples (e.g., chat history, repeated system prompts) to make concrete.
- For quantization, include a small tooltip that explains 8-bit vs 4-bit tradeoffs and a 'View sample output' link to open a side-by-side example.
- Assets should avoid hero imagery that implies vendor lock-in; keep styling neutral, engineering-focused (monochrome plus accent).
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Too much technical detail will overwhelm first-time users. Mitigation: provide 'Advanced details' toggle in the prototype; default canvas stays high-level.
Risk: Engineering constraints change (runtime changes API labels). Mitigation: sync with ENG-7291 and freeze copy before handoff (cutoff date 2025-03-05).
notes_for_engineering:
- Export constraints: 2x PNG at 1600px width for desktop, 800px for narrow, 360px for mobile.
- Provide layer names that map to Console components for easier handoff.
- Include CSS color tokens in Figma styles.
- Provide small JSON manifest describing the annotated callouts for automatic import into docs generator.
review_checklist:

- [ ] Engineering feasibility review (ENG-7291)
- [ ] Accessibility pass (contrast and alt text)
- [ ] Figma prototype link in PR
- [ ] Assets uploaded to Drive
